content: Psychosocial care should be made available to every individual diagnosed with diabetes to enhance their overall quality of life and improve health outcomes. This type of care should be integrated into the standard management of diabetes and may address various concerns such as stress, quality of life, depression, and cognitive difficulties. Patients with diabetes should undergo routine psychological screenings at least once a year, as well as during any significant changes in their health status, to identify potential psychological issues. If specific psychological concerns arise, such as symptoms of emotional distress, clinical depression, or disordered eating behaviors, patients should be referred to qualified behavioral health professionals for specialized care. Healthcare providers should utilize evidence-based tools and strategies that have been validated for use in individuals with diabetes to deliver effective psychosocial support tailored to their needs.
